Algebra I · Lesson 9.5

Factoring in Action

Solve this lesson →All lessons

The equation x4−20x2+64=0x4−20x2+64=0 has degree four, so it is not a quadratic. But x4=(x2)2x4=(x2)2, so the only powers of xx in it are x2x2 and the square of x2x2. Write uu for x2x2. The equation is then u2−20u+64=0u2−20u+64=0, which 9.2's search factors as (u−4)(u−16)=0(u−4)(u−16)=0, so x2=4x2=4 or x2=16x2=16, and x=±2x=±2 or x=±4x=±4.

Problem
Solve x4−34x2+225=0x4−34x2+225=0. Write uu for x2x2, factor the quadratic in uu, then go back to xx. Enter the largest of the four solutions.
Show a hint
  • Since x4=(x2)2x4=(x2)2, writing uu for x2x2 turns the equation into u2−34u+225=0u2−34u+225=0.
  • Two numbers with product 225225 and sum −34−34 are −9−9 and −25−25, so x2=9x2=9 or x2=25x2=25. Each of those has two solutions.
Show the full solution
With u=x2u=x2 the equation is u2−34u+225=0u2−34u+225=0, and two numbers with product 225225 and sum −34−34 are −9−9 and −25−25, so it factors as (u−9)(u−25)=0(u−9)(u−25)=0. Then x2=9x2=9 gives x=±3x=±3 and x2=25x2=25 gives x=±5x=±5, so the largest of the four is 55​. The values 99 and 2525 are values of x2x2, so neither is a solution of the original equation.
Problem
In (2x+3)2−14(2x+3)+40=0(2x+3)2−14(2x+3)+40=0 the expression 2x+32x+3 appears squared and again on its own. Write uu for 2x+32x+3, solve for uu, then solve for xx. Enter the larger value of xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The repeated piece does not have to be a power of xx. Here it is 2x+32x+3, so the equation is u2−14u+40=0u2−14u+40=0.
  • u2−14u+40=(u−4)(u−10)u2−14u+40=(u−4)(u−10), so 2x+3=42x+3=4 or 2x+3=102x+3=10. Subtract 33, then divide by 22.
Show the full solution
Writing uu for 2x+32x+3 gives u2−14u+40=0u2−14u+40=0, which factors as (u−4)(u−10)=0(u−4)(u−10)=0. Then 2x+3=42x+3=4 gives x=12x=21​, and 2x+3=102x+3=10 gives x=72x=27​, so the larger value is 7227​​. Both 44 and 1010 are values of uu, not of xx, so neither one is a solution until the substitution is undone.
Key idea
A quadratic in a repeated piece. An equation is a quadratic in some expression when that expression appears squared, appears once more with only a number multiplying it, and nothing else in the equation contains the variable. Write a single letter for it, say uu, and what is left is au2+bu+c=0au2+bu+c=0, which 9.2's search and 9.3's split already factor. Nothing else changes. x4−20x2+64=0x4−20x2+64=0 and u2−20u+64=0u2−20u+64=0 are the same string of symbols once x2x2 is written as uu, and the same holds for (2x+3)2−14(2x+3)+40=0(2x+3)2−14(2x+3)+40=0, where the piece is 2x+32x+3 rather than a power.
Problem
Solve (x−6)2−2(x−6)−24=0(x−6)2−2(x−6)−24=0 and enter the larger solution. The expression x−6x−6 repeats, so give that repeated piece a single letter before you factor.
Show a hint
  • Write u=x−6u=x−6. The equation becomes u2−2u−24=0u2−2u−24=0, which needs two numbers with product −24−24 and sum −2−2.
  • The factoring gives (u−6)(u+4)=0(u−6)(u+4)=0, so u=6u=6 or u=−4u=−4. Now recover xx from each value of uu, then take the larger.
Show the full solution
With u=x−6u=x−6 the equation is u2−2u−24=(u−6)(u+4)=0u2−2u−24=(u−6)(u+4)=0, so u=6u=6 or u=−4u=−4. Those are values of x−6x−6, so x=12x=12 or x=2x=2, and the larger is 1212​. Reporting 66 is the common mistake. It is the larger value of uu, and uu stands for x−6x−6.
Problem
Solve x4−13x2−48=0x4−13x2−48=0 by writing uu for x2x2. How many real solutions does the equation have? Enter a single number.
Show a hint
  • The equation in uu is u2−13u−48=0u2−13u−48=0. Solve that first and read off both values of uu.
  • The values are u=16u=16 and u=−3u=−3. Ask which real numbers satisfy x2=16x2=16, and which satisfy x2=−3x2=−3.
Show the full solution
In uu the equation is u2−13u−48=0u2−13u−48=0, and two numbers with product −48−48 and sum −13−13 are −16−16 and 33, so it factors as (u−16)(u+3)=0(u−16)(u+3)=0. Then x2=16x2=16 gives x=4x=4 and x=−4x=−4, while x2=−3x2=−3 has no real solution, since no real number squares to a negative. The count is 22​. Two values of uu do not automatically mean four values of xx.
Key idea
Undoing the substitution. A value of uu is not a solution. Since uu stands for a piece built from xx, setting that piece equal to the value leaves one more equation to solve. When the piece is x2x2, a positive value of uu gives two values of xx, u=0u=0 gives one, and a negative value gives none, so the number of real solutions can be four, three, two, one or none. When the piece is linear, such as x−6x−6 or 2x+32x+3, each value of uu gives exactly one xx. Count the solutions after the undo step, never before it.

The repeated piece is not always obvious. In 1x2−11x+24=0x21​−x11​+24=0 it is 1xx1​, since 1x2=(1x)2x21​=(x1​)2, and u2−11u+24=(u−3)(u−8)u2−11u+24=(u−3)(u−8) gives 1x=3x1​=3 or 88, so x=13x=31​ or x=18x=81​. Multiplying the original by x2x2 gives 24x2−11x+1=024x2−11x+1=0, with the same two roots.

Problem
Solve x+56x=18x+x56​=18. Multiply both sides by xx, collect everything on one side, and factor. Enter the larger solution.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying by xx turns 56xx56​ into 5656 and xx into x2x2, so no fraction is left.
  • The cleared equation is x2−18x+56=0x2−18x+56=0. Two numbers with product 5656 and sum −18−18 are −4−4 and −14−14.
Show the full solution
Multiplying by xx gives x2+56=18xx2+56=18x, so x2−18x+56=0x2−18x+56=0, which factors as (x−4)(x−14)=0(x−4)(x−14)=0. The solutions are 44 and 1414, so the larger is 1414​. Both check in the original equation, and x=0x=0 is not a candidate, since 560056​ is not a number.
Problem
Solve 4x−2+xx+2=16x2−4x−24​+x+2x​=x2−416​, where x2−4=(x−2)(x+2)x2−4=(x−2)(x+2). Multiplying through by (x−2)(x+2)(x−2)(x+2) produces two candidates, and only one of them solves the original equation. Enter that one.
Show a hint
  • Multiply every term by (x−2)(x+2)(x−2)(x+2). In the first term the x−2x−2 divides out, in the second the x+2x+2 does, and on the right both do.
  • You get 4(x+2)+x(x−2)=164(x+2)+x(x−2)=16, so x2+2x−8=0x2+2x−8=0. Factor it, then put each candidate into 4x−2x−24​ before deciding.
Show the full solution
Multiplying every term by (x−2)(x+2)(x−2)(x+2) gives 4(x+2)+x(x−2)=164(x+2)+x(x−2)=16, so x2+2x−8=0x2+2x−8=0 and (x+4)(x−2)=0(x+4)(x−2)=0. The candidates are −4−4 and 22. At x=2x=2 the denominator x−2x−2 is zero, so 22 is not a solution, and the answer is −4−4​. Checking, 4−6+−4−2=43−64​+−2−4​=34​, which matches 16121216​.
Key idea
Clearing denominators. Multiplying both sides of an equation by an expression that contains xx is legal only where that expression is not zero. Away from those values, the cleared equation has exactly the solutions the original has. At those values the original is undefined while the cleared equation can still be true, so a candidate reached by correct algebra can still fail to solve the original. Such a candidate is extraneous. Write down the values that make a denominator zero before clearing, and drop any candidate that matches one.

A numerator and a denominator can share a factor. Since x2+3x−18=(x+6)(x−3)x2+3x−18=(x+6)(x−3), the expression x2+3x−18x−3x−3x2+3x−18​ equals x+6x+6 at every value of xx except 33. At x=3x=3 the original is 0000​ and has no value, while x+6x+6 is 99. Cancelling a factor leaves the excluded value excluded.

Problem
Solve x2−3x−10x+2=−7x+2x2−3x−10​=−7. The numerator factors, and one of its factors is the denominator. How many solutions does the equation have? Enter a single number.
Show a hint
  • x2−3x−10=(x−5)(x+2)x2−3x−10=(x−5)(x+2), so for every xx except −2−2 the left side equals x−5x−5.
  • That leaves x−5=−7x−5=−7, so the only candidate is x=−2x=−2. Check that value against the original denominator.
Show the full solution
Since x2−3x−10=(x−5)(x+2)x2−3x−10=(x−5)(x+2), the left side equals x−5x−5 wherever it is defined, and x−5=−7x−5=−7 gives x=−2x=−2. But x=−2x=−2 makes the denominator zero, so it is not a solution and the count is 00​. Multiplying through instead gives x2−3x−10=−7x−14x2−3x−10=−7x−14, so x2+4x+4=0x2+4x+4=0 and (x+2)(x+2)=0(x+2)(x+2)=0, the same excluded candidate again.
Fun fact
Ludovico Ferrari solved the general fourth-degree equation around 1540, while still in his teens. His method introduces one new quantity, and finding that quantity takes only a third-degree equation, which was already solvable.
Problem
The numbers aa and bb satisfy 3a2−11ab+6b2=03a2−11ab+6b2=0, and bb is not zero. Read the left side as a quadratic in aa, with bb held as a constant, and factor it. Enter the smaller of the two possible values of abba​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • As a quadratic in aa the three coefficients are 33, −11b−11b and 6b26b2. Each factor has an aa term and a bb term.
  • Use the middle-term split from 9.3. Multiply 3a23a2 by 6b26b2 to get 18a2b218a2b2, break −11ab−11ab into two terms with that product, then group in pairs. Set each factor to zero and divide by bb.
Show the full solution
As a quadratic in aa, 3a2−11ab+6b2=(3a−2b)(a−3b)=03a2−11ab+6b2=(3a−2b)(a−3b)=0, so 3a=2b3a=2b or a=3ba=3b. Dividing by bb, which is not zero, gives ab=23ba​=32​ or ab=3ba​=3, and the smaller is 2332​​. Dividing the original equation by b2b2 is the second route, since 3t2−11t+6=03t2−11t+6=0 with t=abt=ba​ has the same two solutions.
Key idea
A quadratic in one of several letters. An equation in two letters is a quadratic in aa when aa appears squared, appears once on its own, and nowhere else. The three coefficients are then built from the other letter. In 3a2−11ab+6b2=03a2−11ab+6b2=0 they are 33, −11b−11b and 6b26b2, and 9.3's split runs unchanged, with one bb in each factor. Setting a factor to zero gives aa as a multiple of bb rather than as a number, so neither letter has a value of its own here. Each factor gives one of the two possible values of abba​.

Several routes are open now. If the equation is already ax2+bx+c=0ax2+bx+c=0, factor it and take a root from each factor. If one piece repeats, name it, solve, then undo the name. If the variable sits under a fraction bar, clear the denominators first. If the question asks only for the sum or the product, read it off the coefficients with 9.4's two facts.

Problem
A cyclist covers 6060 kilometres at a steady speed. At 55 kilometres per hour faster the ride would have taken one hour less, so her speed vv satisfies 60v−60v+5=1v60​−v+560​=1. Find vv in kilometres per hour.
Show a hint
  • Multiply both sides by v(v+5)v(v+5). On the left the first term becomes 60(v+5)60(v+5) and the second becomes 60v60v, and the right side becomes v(v+5)v(v+5).
  • That gives 300=v2+5v300=v2+5v, so v2+5v−300=0v2+5v−300=0. Factor it, then ask which of the two candidates can be a speed.
Show the full solution
Multiplying by v(v+5)v(v+5) gives 60(v+5)−60v=v(v+5)60(v+5)−60v=v(v+5), so 300=v2+5v300=v2+5v and v2+5v−300=0v2+5v−300=0, which factors as (v−15)(v+20)=0(v−15)(v+20)=0. The roots are 1515 and −20−20, and a speed cannot be negative, so v=15v=15​. The root −20−20 solves the equation exactly, so it is ruled out by what vv measures and not by the algebra. Checking, 6015−6020=4−3=11560​−2060​=4−3=1.
Problem
Clearing the denominators in 5x+5x−4=3x5​+x−45​=3 gives 3x2−22x+20=03x2−22x+20=0, which has no integer factorization, so no method in this chapter produces either solution. Find the sum of the two solutions of the original equation as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • 9.4 gives the sum of the roots as −ba−ab​, read straight off the coefficients with no factoring.
  • Here a=3a=3 and b=−22b=−22. Before using them, check that neither excluded value, 00 or 44, is a root of the cleared quadratic.
Show the full solution
For 3x2−22x+203x2−22x+20 the sum of the roots is −ba=−−223=223−ab​=−3−22​=322​​. Neither excluded value is a root, since 3x2−22x+203x2−22x+20 equals 2020 at x=0x=0 and −20−20 at x=4x=4, so both roots of the quadratic solve the original equation. Factoring is not needed here, since the question asks about the two solutions together.
Key idea
Choosing the tool. In chapter 9, factoring with the zero product property is the only route to the individual solutions, and it needs standard form and an integer factorization. For a question about the two solutions together, 9.4's sum and product come straight from the coefficients, factorable or not. Substitution puts an equation that is a quadratic in some piece into the first case, at the cost of undoing the name afterwards. Clearing denominators does the same for a variable under a fraction bar, at the cost of a check against the excluded values.

Substitution helps only when the quadratic it produces factors, and plenty do not. In x4−7x2+5=0x4−7x2+5=0 the substitution gives u2−7u+5=0u2−7u+5=0, and the only integer pairs with product 55 sum to 66 or −6−6, never −7−7. Chapter 10 adds factorizations chapter 9 has no name for, and chapter 11 gives a method that solves every quadratic.

Problem
Solve (x2+2x)2=2x2+4x+3(x2+2x)2=2x2+4x+3. The right side contains a copy of the piece that is squared on the left. Enter the smallest real solution.
Show a hint
  • 2x2+4x=2(x2+2x)2x2+4x=2(x2+2x), so the right side is 2(x2+2x)+32(x2+2x)+3.
  • With u=x2+2xu=x2+2x the equation is u2=2u+3u2=2u+3, so u2−2u−3=0u2−2u−3=0 and u=3u=3 or u=−1u=−1. Each value gives its own quadratic in xx.
Show the full solution
Since 2x2+4x=2(x2+2x)2x2+4x=2(x2+2x), the equation is u2=2u+3u2=2u+3 with u=x2+2xu=x2+2x, so u2−2u−3=(u−3)(u+1)=0u2−2u−3=(u−3)(u+1)=0 and u=3u=3 or u=−1u=−1. Then x2+2x−3=0x2+2x−3=0 gives x=1x=1 and x=−3x=−3, and x2+2x+1=0x2+2x+1=0 gives x=−1x=−1, so the smallest is −3−3​. There are three distinct solutions, not four, because the second value of uu gives a repeated factor.
Problem
Solve (2xx−1)2−16(2xx−1)+28=0(x−12x​)2−16(x−12x​)+28=0. One of the two values of the repeated piece produces no value of xx at all. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Write uu for 2xx−1x−12x​. The equation is u2−16u+28=0u2−16u+28=0.
  • u2−16u+28=(u−2)(u−14)u2−16u+28=(u−2)(u−14). For u=2u=2, multiply out 2x=2(x−1)2x=2(x−1) and see what is left. Then do u=14u=14.
Show the full solution
With u=2xx−1u=x−12x​ the equation is u2−16u+28=(u−2)(u−14)=0u2−16u+28=(u−2)(u−14)=0, so u=2u=2 or u=14u=14. For u=2u=2, 2x=2(x−1)2x=2(x−1) gives 0=−20=−2, which no xx satisfies. For u=14u=14, 2x=14(x−1)2x=14(x−1) gives 12x=1412x=14, so x=76x=67​​. Two values of uu can still leave one solution, and here that is because 2xx−1x−12x​ is never equal to 22.

Every equation in this lesson was a quadratic in something, a renamed piece or xx itself once the denominators were cleared, and chapter 9's tools were enough. Chapter 10, Special Factorizations, adds factorizations this chapter has no name for, sums and differences of cubes among them, recognized by shape rather than found by a search.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The expression x2+x−56x+8x+8x2+x−56​ equals x−7x−7 at every value of xx but one. Enter the value of xx where the expression is undefined.
Show the solution
The denominator is zero at x=−8x=−8​. Since x2+x−56=(x+8)(x−7)x2+x−56=(x+8)(x−7), cancelling x+8x+8 leaves x−7x−7, which is −15−15 there, while the original is 0000​ and has no value. Cancelling is legal only where x+8x+8 is not zero, so that one value stays excluded.
Practice
Solve x4−53x2+196=0x4−53x2+196=0 by writing uu for x2x2. Enter the largest value of xx that solves it.
Show the solution
With u=x2u=x2 the equation is u2−53u+196=0u2−53u+196=0, which factors as (u−4)(u−49)=0(u−4)(u−49)=0, so x2=4x2=4 or x2=49x2=49 and the largest value of xx is 77​. The four solutions are −7−7, −2−2, 22 and 77, so stopping at u=49u=49 reports the square of the answer.
Practice
Solve (x+5)2−5(x+5)+4=0(x+5)2−5(x+5)+4=0, where the repeated piece is x+5x+5. Enter the larger value of xx.
Show the solution
With u=x+5u=x+5, (u−1)(u−4)=0(u−1)(u−4)=0 gives u=1u=1 or u=4u=4, so x=−4x=−4 or x=−1x=−1, and the larger is −1−1​. Both values of uu are positive while both solutions are negative, which is why the undo step cannot be skipped.
Practice
Solve x4−8x2−9=0x4−8x2−9=0. Enter the positive solution.
Show the solution
With u=x2u=x2 the equation is u2−8u−9=0u2−8u−9=0, which factors as (u−9)(u+1)=0(u−9)(u+1)=0, so u=9u=9 or u=−1u=−1. No real number squares to −1−1, and x2=9x2=9 gives x=±3x=±3, so the positive solution is 33​. The value 99 is x2x2 rather than xx, so it is not itself a solution.
Practice
Solve 54x=x+3x54​=x+3 by multiplying both sides by xx. Enter the positive solution.
Show the solution
Multiplying by xx gives 54=x2+3x54=x2+3x, so x2+3x−54=0x2+3x−54=0 and (x+9)(x−6)=0(x+9)(x−6)=0. The solutions are −9−9 and 66, so the positive one is 66​. Neither is 00, so both are legal values of xx in the original equation.
Practice
Solve x2−12x+27x−9=5x−9x2−12x+27​=5. The numerator shares a factor with the denominator. Enter the solution.
Show the solution
Since x2−12x+27=(x−3)(x−9)x2−12x+27=(x−3)(x−9), the left side equals x−3x−3 wherever the expression is defined, so x−3=5x−3=5 and x=8x=8​. The excluded value is 99, and 88 is not it, so this candidate survives.
Practice
How many different real values of xx satisfy x4+9x2=0x4+9x2=0? Enter a single number.
Show the solution
With u=x2u=x2 the equation is u2+9u=0u2+9u=0, so u(u+9)=0u(u+9)=0 and u=0u=0 or u=−9u=−9. Then x2=0x2=0 gives only x=0x=0, and x2=−9x2=−9 gives no real xx, so the count is 11​. A uu of zero is the one case that yields a single xx, since a positive uu yields two and a negative uu none.
Practice
The square of a positive integer plus twice that integer is 288288. Enter the integer.
Show the solution
With nn the integer, n2+2n=288n2+2n=288, so n2+2n−288=0n2+2n−288=0 and (n−16)(n+18)=0(n−16)(n+18)=0. The roots are 1616 and −18−18, and the integer has to be positive, so it is 1616​. Checking, 256+32=288256+32=288.
Practice
Clearing the denominators in xx+5+2x=3x+5x​+x2​=3 gives 2x2+13x−10=02x2+13x−10=0, which has no integer factorization. Neither 00 nor −5−5 is a root of it. Enter the sum of the two solutions as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
For 2x2+13x−102x2+13x−10 the sum of the roots is −ba=−132−ab​=−213​, so the sum of the two solutions is −132−213​​. The excluded values 00 and −5−5 are not roots, so nothing is discarded and no factorization is needed.
Practice
Solve (4x+3)2−7(4x+3)−8=0(4x+3)2−7(4x+3)−8=0. Enter the larger solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
With u=4x+3u=4x+3 the equation is (u−8)(u+1)=0(u−8)(u+1)=0, so 4x+3=84x+3=8 or 4x+3=−14x+3=−1, which give x=54x=45​ and x=−1x=−1, and the larger is 5445​​. Stopping at u=8u=8 is the usual slip, since 88 is a value of the repeated piece and not a value of xx.
Practice
Solve 4x4−17x2+4=04x4−17x2+4=0 by writing uu for x2x2. Enter the smallest positive solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
With u=x2u=x2, 4u2−17u+4=(4u−1)(u−4)=04u2−17u+4=(4u−1)(u−4)=0, so u=14u=41​ or u=4u=4. Undoing the substitution, x2=14x2=41​ gives x=±12x=±21​ and x2=4x2=4 gives x=±2x=±2, so the smallest positive solution is 1221​​. Each positive uu gives two values of xx, which is why a quadratic in x2x2 can have four solutions.
Practice
Solve x+5x−6=66x2−6xx−6x+5​=x2−6x66​. The denominator on the right factors as x(x−6)x(x−6), and one of the two candidates is extraneous. Enter the single value of xx that solves the equation.
Show the solution
Multiplying by x(x−6)x(x−6) gives x(x+5)=66x(x+5)=66, so x2+5x−66=0x2+5x−66=0 and (x+11)(x−6)=0(x+11)(x−6)=0. The candidates are −11−11 and 66, and x=6x=6 makes both original denominators zero, so the solution is −11−11​. Checking, −6−17=617−17−6​=176​ and 66187=61718766​=176​.
Practice
Solve 6x−1+xx+1=12x2−1x−16​+x+1x​=x2−112​. The denominator on the right factors as (x−1)(x+1)(x−1)(x+1), and one candidate makes a denominator zero. Enter the solution.
Show the solution
Multiplying by (x−1)(x+1)(x−1)(x+1) gives 6(x+1)+x(x−1)=126(x+1)+x(x−1)=12, so x2+5x−6=0x2+5x−6=0 and (x+6)(x−1)=0(x+6)(x−1)=0. The candidates are −6−6 and 11, and x=1x=1 makes x−1x−1 zero, so the solution is −6−6​.
Practice
The numbers aa and bb satisfy 2a2−9ab+10b2=02a2−9ab+10b2=0, and bb is not zero. Enter the larger of the two possible values of abba​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
As a quadratic in aa, (2a−5b)(a−2b)=0(2a−5b)(a−2b)=0, so 2a=5b2a=5b or a=2ba=2b. Dividing by bb gives ab=52ba​=25​ or ab=2ba​=2, and the larger is 5225​​. Both are genuinely possible, since (a,b)=(5,2)(a,b)=(5,2) and (a,b)=(2,1)(a,b)=(2,1) each satisfy the equation.
Practice
The numbers aa and bb satisfy 4a2+4ab−3b2=04a2+4ab−3b2=0, and bb is not zero. Enter the smaller of the two possible values of abba​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
As a quadratic in aa, the left side factors as (2a−b)(2a+3b)(2a−b)(2a+3b), so 2a=b2a=b or 2a=−3b2a=−3b. Dividing each by bb gives ab=12ba​=21​ or ab=−32ba​=−23​, and the smaller of the two is −32−23​​. Dividing the original equation by b2b2 is the same route, since with t=abt=ba​ it reads 4t2+4t−3=04t2+4t−3=0.
Practice
Solve (x2+8x)2+6(x2+8x)−135=0(x2+8x)2+6(x2+8x)−135=0. Each value of the repeated piece gives a quadratic that factors over the integers. Enter the sum of all four solutions.
Show the solution
With u=x2+8xu=x2+8x, (u−9)(u+15)=0(u−9)(u+15)=0 gives u=9u=9 or u=−15u=−15. Then x2+8x−9=0x2+8x−9=0 gives x=1x=1 and x=−9x=−9, and x2+8x+15=0x2+8x+15=0 gives x=−3x=−3 and x=−5x=−5, so the sum is 1−9−3−5=−161−9−3−5=−16​. Both quadratics have the form x2+8x+kx2+8x+k and both have real roots, so by 9.4 each pair of roots sums to −8−8 and the total is twice −8−8.
Practice
Solve (x+1x−1)2−11(x+1x−1)+10=0(x−1x+1​)2−11(x−1x+1​)+10=0. One value of the repeated piece produces no xx at all. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
With u=x+1x−1u=x−1x+1​, (u−1)(u−10)=0(u−1)(u−10)=0 gives u=1u=1 or u=10u=10. For u=1u=1, x+1=x−1x+1=x−1 reduces to 1=−11=−1, so no xx works. For u=10u=10, x+1=10x−10x+1=10x−10 gives 9x=119x=11, so x=119x=911​​.
